title: What Happens When Doing Nothing Burns Nearly All Its Fuel?
description:
Clinical Case Briefing — Marcus Raichle (2001): The Default Mode Network & 'Brain Dark Energy' Burning 20% of Your Body's Fuel at Rest, grounded in Marcus E. Raichle, Ann Mary MacLeod, Abraham Z. Snyder, William J. Powers et al. (2001) (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences). Empirical findings show that for decades, brain-imaging labs treated lying quietly in a scanner with eyes closed ('rest') as a blank zero baseline — throwing away strange negative numbers whenever certain regions went DOWN during math or reading tasks.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how default mode network, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that at Washington University in St. Louis, Gordon Shulman and Marcus Raichle refused to throw out those 'deactivations': across 9 different PET studies (132 subjects), the EXACT SAME constellation of midline/parietal regions consistently turned DOWN whenever people switched from quiet rest to an external task.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Marcus E. Raichle, Ann Mary MacLeod, Abraham Z. Snyder, William J. Powers et al. (2001). A default mode of brain function. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.98.2.676
- Marcus E. Raichle (2015). The Brain's Default Mode Network. Annual Review of Neuroscience. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-neuro-071013-014030
- Debra Gusnard, Erbil Akbudak, Gordon Shulman, Marcus E. Raichle (2001). Role of medial prefrontal cortex in a default mode of brain function. NeuroImage. https://doi.org/10.1016/s1053-8119(01)91757-4

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
